title: Quantum Computing: Algorithms, Architectures, and Applications
abstract_summary: This edited book provides a comprehensive overview of quantum computing, covering foundational principles (qubits, gates, circuits), core quantum algorithms (e.g., Shor's, Grover's, variational algorithms), and hardware architectures including superconducting qubits, trapped ions, and photonic systems. It balances theory and practice with discussions on error correction, NISQ devices, quantum-classical hybrid frameworks, and applications across cryptography, optimization, AI, materials science, healthcare, and finance, aimed at postgraduate students, researchers, and professionals.
methodology_description: This work is a multi-author, descriptive and integrative academic volume rather than an empirical research paper. The methodology reflected in the preface and acknowledgements is primarily a structured literature synthesis and expert-authored chapter development: domain specialists contributed focused chapters on foundational principles (quantum mechanics, qubits, gates, circuit models), core algorithms (e.g., Shor, Grover, variational methods), hardware architectures (superconducting qubits, trapped ions, photonics), error correction techniques, and application case studies. The editors emphasize a balanced integration of theory and practice by presenting mathematical formulations alongside conceptual explanations, diagrams, case studies, and discussions of contemporary research developments (including NISQ devices and quantum cloud platforms). Peer review and internal academic feedback from contributing institutions supported iterative refinement of chapters. The volume is intended as an instructional and reference text (postgraduate students, faculty, researchers) and does not describe a unified empirical experimental methodology, datasets, or reproducible code artifacts within the provided front-matter text.
